proof: Use the actual frozen labeled cube coordinates A=(0,0,0),B=(1,0,0),C=(1,1,0),D=(0,1,0). M=(1/2,0,0),N=(1,1,1/2). Their plane is 2x+y-4z=1. It also meets BF at P=(1,0,1/4); complete section is D-M-P-N, not triangle D-M-N. The small solid has height (2x+y-1)/4 over 0<=x<=1, max(0,1-2x)<=y<=1. The exact two integrals on x=[0,1/2] and[1/2,1] are1/96 and13/96, totaling7/48. Larger=41/48, hence89. Treating P as a midpoint is inconsistent with the given three-point plane; an explicit fake midpoint/equality is forbidden. Merely drawing the true quarter intersection and assigning it the same color as M would not define one geometrically consistent wrong plane or one defensible new wrong volume.
